Make a server-streaming gRPC call

Source: R/stream.R
grpc_stream.Rd

Sends one request message and returns a stream that yields the response messages one at a time, as they arrive. The server sends only as far ahead as you read, so a stream you stop reading holds the server back rather than filling memory.

Usage

grpc_stream(channel, method, request, metadata = NULL, deadline = NULL)

Arguments

channel

A channel from grpc_channel().

method

The full method name, "/package.Service/Method".

request

The encoded request message, a raw vector.

metadata

Request metadata: a named character vector, or a named list whose -bin entries are raw vectors. Names are lower-cased. Names starting with grpc-, te and content-type are reserved.

deadline

Seconds from now, or an absolute POSIXct, by which the whole stream must end. It is sent as grpc-timeout. Locally it is checked before each read, and each wait for more data is bounded by the time the deadline allowed when the call began, so a stall can overrun a deadline that is already partly used. NULL sets no deadline.

Value

A zugrpc_stream.

Details

The stream is an object with five methods:

  • $headers() returns the initial metadata, a named list.

  • $next_message() returns the next message as a raw vector, or NULL at the end of the stream. It raises a condition, as grpc_call() does, when the call ends with a status other than OK.

  • $trailers() returns the trailing metadata once $next_message() has returned NULL, and NULL before.

  • $status() returns the final status name, such as "OK", once the stream has ended, and NULL before.

  • $cancel() stops the call. The connection stays open for other calls. A second $cancel() does nothing. A later $next_message() raises zugrpc_error_cancelled.

A stream that is no longer referenced is cancelled when it is garbage-collected, and grpc_close() cancels every open stream of its channel.

Examples

# A test server, from zuhttp's mock transport: it streams two messages
# and ends with status OK.
fake <- zuhttp::zu_mock_transport(function(req) {
  zuhttp::zu_response(
    200L,
    headers = c("content-type" = "application/grpc+proto"),
    body = as.raw(c(0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0x61, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0x62)),
    trailers = c("grpc-status" = "0")
  )
})
ch <- grpc_channel(
  "http://localhost:50051",
  client = zuhttp::zu_client(transport = fake)
)
st <- grpc_stream(ch, "/grpc.testing.TestService/StreamingOutputCall", raw())
while (!is.null(m <- st$next_message())) print(rawToChar(m))
#> [1] "a"
#> [1] "b"
st$status()
#> [1] "OK"
